𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐆𝐈, 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐥𝐞𝐲 𝐊𝐮𝐛𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐤. 🪐⁣⁣
⁣⁣
58 years later, 𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟏: 𝐀 𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐎𝐝𝐲𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐲 (𝟏𝟗𝟔𝟖) still looks like something from the future. A film so far ahead of its time that it’s almost impossible to believe it was made before humans even landed on the Moon.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
With no computer-generated imagery, Kubrick relied on practical effects, detailed miniature models, groundbreaking camera techniques, and an almost obsessive attention to detail. The result? Space sequences that still put many modern blockbusters to shame.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
But what makes 2001 even more fascinating is how accurately it anticipated our relationship with technology.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
At the center of the story is HAL 9000, an artificial intelligence designed to assist astronauts on their mission. But when HAL begins making decisions that conflict with human interests, the technology meant to protect them becomes their greatest threat. More than half a century before today’s debates about AI, Kubrick was already asking a terrifying question: What happens when the machines we create become too powerful for us to control?⁣
